questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location and infrastructure -- Madison has a lot of bike baths, a nice winter with lots of snow, etc. Also academics --- they have good engineering and comp sci departments with lots of courses to choose from. I also had friends and family in the area that I wanted to see and visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. I needed help with finding the right courses and figuring out alternatives to the courses I was waitlisted for, and it took a lot of back and forth until I found the right advisor for that. Other more practical things were easier to get help for.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Got help from International Student Services for practical stuff and from the office of Study Abroad for academic advising.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easier if you look further away from campus. There are free bus passes for students as well as bike paths, so it can be worth it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The buses are a bit unreliable and often late, so you need to get an early start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very clear and all online.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Getting all you info in MyUW and Terra Dotta, completing an introductory little course in Canvas.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Detailed instructions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, but I was waitlisted for them and was not sure until the end that it would be possible. But in general it seems like most classes have a high turnover and you have a good chance of making it from the waitlist.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of the waitlists -- your chances are good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really depends on the course. I was extremely pleased with my course in psychology (language comprehension), which is probably one of my favorite courses of all my studies. The engineering courses about machine learning were quite different from what I was used to, and I didn't enjoy them as much -- especially Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks. I still think I learned a lot, but the tests were really tough and the material was presented in a confusing and rushed way.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
PSYCH 711 definitely felt like a masters-level course, very good level and very research-focused
ECE 539 and 532 are more like BA-courses if you already have a technical background, but for IT and Cognition students like me, who don't all have that background, the level felt quite appropriate. I was definitely challenged and didn't do that well on all the tests. However, the grading is based on a lot of other coursework as well, so you can make up for it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The main difference for me was the grading, since I'm used to one project or exam making up the whole grade. Here we had midterms, or multiple tests and/or projects, so there was a lot of "making up for" a bad grade, and just doing the homework basically puts at "passed" level. But there really is a lot of homework and I did feel busier than in UCPH on a daily basis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYCH 711 Advanced Topics in Psychology (Language Comprehension in Adults and Children)
ECE 532 Matrix Methods in Machine Learning
ECE 539 Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
PSYCH 711 with Maryellen Macdonald was EXCELLENT, but the topics and instructor change, so I'm not sure it will be available in the same form going forward. 
ECE 532 was a great foundation for machine learning that I really needed, and the instruction was very clear and helpful. 
ECE 539 was a confusing and frustrating course that I don't recommend. Teaching style very dull and and not paedagogical, very difficult tests and lots of work.

questions.answer: Clothing! The winter is MUCH colder than in Denmark, and I needed new gloves, coats, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I didn't pay anything for books, as none of my courses had textbooks, it was all online material.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I honestly didn't really have to pursue any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots, sports, gym, libraries, events....

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football games! Hike around the area, maybe water sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go down to Chicago or Milwaukee

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to the international student events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: friendliness, food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: go there early and get everything in order, get advising and ask others about good courses!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Good instructors, good food and new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with academics

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No
